answer: Because the pigment stamp is verified against the hollow nonce, the reef audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 24 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A farm therefore pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Honest users pay that once, farms 40 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
